correctness.rationale: The max-rate model is a positive multiple of f_p after rescaling, with the exact closed amplitude domain stated. For p≤1 strict concavity forces a=0. For p>1 set x=m−a, y=m+a, and S=(p−1)(y^p−x^p)/(p(y^(p−1)−x^(p−1))). In the interior the sign of J' is the sign of i_p−S. Equivalently it is the sign of M_p(z)−m for z=atanh(a/m), since the factors removed in the stationarity equation are positive. The hyperbolic derivative establishes strict monotonicity for p≠2, with endpoints i_p and b_p. In Step 2 the phrase ‘at most one’ must be read for p≠2, as its preceding sentence and the explicit flat p=2 case in Step 4 indicate. For 1<p<2 any interior positive root is a minimum, and comparing the endpoints gives c_p strictly between i_p and b_p, with precisely two maximizers at equality. For p>2 the root is a maximum; at m>.5 the warm-end derivative stays negative because f'(1)=−1 and f'(x)>−1 for x<1. The endpoint thresholds have no other equality case. The interior branch tends to b_p at its lower endpoint and to zero only at i_p; its warm temperature y=p[1−(r−1)/(r^p−1)]/(p+1), r=y/x, decreases as m increases because r decreases and (r^p−1)/(r−1) increases in r. Thus a=y−m indeed decreases there. The expansion S=m+(p−2)a²/(3m)+O(a⁴) confirms the exact onset coefficient. The polynomial identities at p=2 and p=3 give the flat interval and example gain exactly. Read VERIFICATION.md and checks/verify.py without executing them; an independent amplitude grid spanning 13 exponents and 99 means found no violation in 310167 comparisons. This does not replace the analytic boundary and uniqueness checks.

evidence: Along fixed x+y=2m, S increases if p>2 and decreases if 1<p<2 by Theorem A5. The monotonicity is strict away from p=2 because S is analytic for 0<a<m and its expansion m+(p−2)a²/(3m)+O(a⁴) is nonconstant. For a>0, 2J' equals p(p+1)/(p−1) times (y^(p−1)−x^(p−1))(i_p−S), so monotone S gives all derivative sign patterns.

The endpoint values are S(m,m)=m and S(0,2m)=2m(p−1)/p, yielding i_p and b_p. When the feasible warm end is y=1 the derivative there is negative. For 1<p<2 only endpoints can maximize, and their difference is m^p[(2^(p−1)−1)−(2^p−1)m]. For p=2 the mean S is exactly m, giving the flat equality case. For p>2 imposing S=i_p and using its displayed expansion gives both the stated stationary equation and a²~3i_p(i_p−m)/(p−2).
